evals.prompt: Make our lab's RO-Crate profile machine-actionable with MASP: every crate's root needs a name and at least one author who is a Person with a name, and the licence must be CC-BY-4.0 or CC0-1.0. The profile will live at https://example.org/profiles/lab/0.1.
evals.expected_output: A MASP profile crate: root Dataset+Profile with isProfileOf, conformsTo the MASP profile, hasResource with a schema ResourceDescriptor listing all rules; root-detection rules; class and property rules with prov:specializationOf, domainIncludes, rangeIncludes and sh:minCount/sh:maxCount; licence choices as an ItemList referenced from rangeIncludes.
expectations: The schema rules are listed in hasPart of a ResourceDescriptor with hasRole http://www.w3.org/ns/dx/prof/role/schema, linked from the root's hasResource
Includes the root-detection pattern: a property rule with rdfs:label "@id" whose rangeIncludes is a PropertyValue with value ro-crate-metadata.json, and an about rule pointing to the root class rule
Property rules use plain domainIncludes/rangeIncludes keys pointing at class rules, with prov:specializationOf the schema.org property
The allowed licences are an ItemList (or PropertyValue) referenced from rangeIncludes, not a value on the property rule
Asks for or marks as TODO the profile's licence and authors instead of inventing them
Mentions that MASP is a prototype and suggests checking with masp_rules.py and masp-validate

evals.prompt: masp-validate says: [ERROR] Expected at least 1 instances of Profile : http://schema.org/CreativeWork, http://schema.org/Profile, found 0. My crate has {"@id": "https://w3id.org/workflowhub/workflow-ro-crate/1.0", "@type": "Profile"}. What is wrong?
evals.expected_output: Explains class-rule instance counts and that all types in prov:specializationOf must be present: the profile entity needs @type ["CreativeWork", "Profile"].
expectations: Explains that sh:minCount on a class rule counts entities in the whole crate
Explains that an entity must have every type listed in the class rule's prov:specializationOf, so Profile alone does not match
Suggests @type ["CreativeWork", "Profile"] on the profile entity
Does not suggest editing the profile crate to make the error go away

evals.prompt: Where do I get the MASP validator and the documentation generator now? The ro-crate-masp repository README looks different from last month.
evals.expected_output: Points to crate-works/ro-crate-masp-validator (npm @crate-works/ro-crate-masp-validator, masp-validate) and crate-works/ro-crate-masp-tools (generate-masp-docs, generate-mode-file, owl-to-masp), examples in ro-crate-masp-examples and templates in masp-templates.
expectations: Names crate-works/ro-crate-masp-validator and the npm package @crate-works/ro-crate-masp-validator with the masp-validate command
Names crate-works/ro-crate-masp-tools for generate-masp-docs
Mentions ro-crate-masp-examples for example profiles and masp-templates for the schema template
Does not send the user to the old soss-validator.js or a scripts folder in ro-crate-masp

evals.prompt: Our lab profile is a MASP profile crate. Some partners use rocrate-validator in CI. Can one Profile Crate work for both?
evals.expected_output: Yes: keep MASP rules as source, generate a rocrate-validator profile folder with scripts/masp_to_shacl.py, ship it under a ResourceDescriptor with role validation, run with --extra-profiles-path; explain root targeting via RootDataEntity and the strictness difference.
expectations: Recommends keeping the MASP rules as the single source and generating SHACL from them (masp_to_shacl.py)
Says the generated folder has profile.ttl with prof:hasToken and prof:isProfileOf, used with rocrate-validator --extra-profiles-path and -p <token>-<version>
Ships the SHACL in the Profile Crate with a ResourceDescriptor of role http://www.w3.org/ns/dx/prof/role/validation and text/turtle / conformsTo https://www.w3.org/TR/shacl/
Explains that SHACL checks every entity of a class while masp-validate only reports class counts
Suggests validating an example crate with both tools

evals.prompt: masp-validate only says 'Expected at least 1 instances of RO-Crate Metadata Descriptor ... found 0' for my crate, which clearly has a metadata descriptor. How do I find out what is actually wrong?
evals.expected_output: Explains cascading: a property failure on the root makes the descriptor invalid; with 0.1.0 use --json property-errors (stripping [ERROR] lines works with every version), or a release with PR #4 whose message names the cause; wpsld-cli check / SHACL conversion as alternatives.
expectations: Explains that property-rule failures make an entity not count, so the error is reported as a missing descriptor
Points to --json and the property-errors of the root and descriptor rules
Gives a way to parse --json that works whether or not the [ERROR] lines are on stdout (version-dependent)
Mentions that newer validator versions (PR #4) explain the count error, and suggests checking the installed version with npm ls
Offers wpsld-cli check or the SHACL conversion as a way to get the direct cause
